theDefectAsUnderstood.theMeasuredShape: The county ring is 10 vertices / 9 edges. Read with the labeller's own rule it resolves to a 4-line lot: three collinear runs of 3+3+2 chords. Chord bearings: e8,e0,e1 all 135.2 deg (2.14 + 42.11 + 3.44 = 47.69 m = ONE long side line); e3,e4,e5 all -44.8 deg (3.53 + 41.98 + 2.10 = 47.61 m = the OPPOSITE long side line); e6,e7 both 45.2 deg (11.50 + 5.29 = 16.79 m = the FAR end line); e2 alone (-134.6 deg, 16.80 m = the NEAR end line, the Sturgeon frontage). Every internal turn inside a run is 0.0 degrees; every real corner turn is ~90 degrees.
theDefectAsUnderstood.whyItCollapsesToAFalseZero: The labeller labels CHORDS, not lot lines, so the sub-chords of one line get DIFFERENT setbacks. Measured consequence on this ring: the same-street corner-clip rule fires on e1 (3.44 m, 9.3 m from Sturgeon) and e3 (3.53 m, 9.4 m from Sturgeon) because each shares a vertex with the front edge e2 and is within CORNER_CLIP_DISTANCE_PARITY_M (|9.3-7.6| = 1.7 m, |9.4-7.6| = 1.8 m), so both become side_corner at 15 ft = 4.57 m — on chords 3.44 m and 3.53 m LONG, i.e. each is asked to inset DEEPER than its own length. The rear lands on e6 (11.50 m) while e7 (5.29 m, collinear with e6, the same far end line) stays side, so one 16.79 m end line carries two different setbacks. The inset offsets that fold are exactly the ones a perimeter offset cannot represent, and the envelope comes back empty — the 'long narrow lot collapses to a false zero' in the dispatch.
theDefectAsUnderstood.theFrontIsNotTheDefectOnThisParcel_AndIS: Measured, and this contradicts the dispatch's prose sentence. The dispatch says the front 'is inferred from the nearest street centerline instead of the situs-named street'. On the live ring it does not: situs '629 STURGEON DR' normalizes to STURGEON (house number dropped, trailing suffix DR dropped) and OSM's 'Sturgeon Street' normalizes to STURGEON (STREET dropped), so the R30 situs path DOES match, and it picks the closest situs-matching edge e2 at 7.6 m — which is also the nearest street (Claire Drive is nearest to e0 at 26.6 m, outside the 25 m threshold, so it never registers). The front is right and the front basis is already situs-street-match. What is wrong is everything AROUND the front: the artifacts, the ungrouped lines, and the resulting collapse. I record the contradiction rather than restating the dispatch's sentence as if I had measured it.
theDefectAsUnderstood.theTwoLabellersReallyDoDiffer: LDT's frontFromShape explicitly excludes slivers under SURVEY_NOISE_THRESHOLD_M from front candidacy and refuses a unique globally-shortest eligible edge when other candidates exist; its rear is max(|cos| x distance) from the front edge midpoint; it never lets a chord's setback be decided by a vertex it shares with the front, because it never has a same-street corner-clip rule at all. The engine instead carries three bespoke flag-lot/corner-clip rules keyed to RAW chord indices (the 31317, 34177 and Mesquite classes). Neither labeller groups chords into lot lines, which is why the dispatch's sentence 'LDT's live labeller does group ring chords into logical edges' is NOT what the LDT source shows — LDT avoids the failure by a different route (sliver exclusion + shape refusal), it does not group. Recorded as a contradiction; the deliverable is unchanged, because the engine side genuinely lacks the grouping and needs it.

theDesign.oneImplementationOrADivergenceTest: The dispatch offers both. Taken: ONE ENGINE IMPLEMENTATION plus a recorded-fixture divergence test, because the shared-primitive branch requires editing legacy-design-tools/buildableEnvelope/ while LDT PRs #701 (P-249) and #702 (P-293) are open on that exact directory. LDT is read, never written. The divergence test runs the SAME two fixtures through this lane's labeller and asserts the answers LDT's labeller produces for the same inputs, recorded by hand from the LDT source with the LDT rule each answer comes from named inline, so a future reader can re-derive it. It is a plain fixture test (P-282's harness does not exist in this clone; P-282 is a factory row).
theDesign.part1_ringScrub: new module depth-warm/ring-logical-edges.ts. validateParcelRing: >= 3 distinct vertices, all coordinates finite, non-zero signed area, no self-intersection -> else the new named decline 'ring-validation-failed'. scrubRingForLabeling: drops exact and near duplicates (DUPLICATE_VERTEX_TOL_M = 0.5) then near-collinear vertices (COLLINEAR_VERTEX_TOL_DEG = 1.0) using the same exact cross-product law lot-line-scrub.ts uses, with the shape-preservation bound the existing scrub already carries, and returns the surviving vertex indices so labels can be mapped back. Reusing the existing scrub's law rather than inventing a second one; the existing scrub is NOT re-parameterised, so the boundary-primitive path is untouched.
theDesign.part2_logicalEdgeGrouping: groupRingChordsIntoLogicalEdges: a maximal run of consecutive chords whose turn at each shared vertex is <= LOGICAL_EDGE_MAX_TURN_DEG (10) is ONE logical edge, carrying its chord indices, its start/end vertex, its length and its bearing. 10 degrees is chosen because it is far above digitisation noise and far below a real corner: on both real fixtures every artifact turn is 0.0-1.5 degrees and every real corner is 89-95 degrees, a 60x margin, so no threshold in the range ~2..~45 degrees changes either fixture. A test asserts that margin, and asserts that a 45-degree turn is NOT merged.
theDesign.part3_frontSelection: the existing situs-first rule is kept exactly as it is (R30/R33 untouched, and the fail-closed declines keep firing on the same conditions), but it is evaluated over LOGICAL edges: the situs-named street still wins, and the edge it wins is the whole lot line, so the front expands to every chord of that line. Curved frontage: a maximal run of consecutive front-eligible chords adjacent to the FRONT's own osmWayId whose consecutive turns are <= CURVED_FRONTAGE_MAX_TURN_DEG (45) and which all share the front's road-distance parity is ONE front. That is the dispatch's item 3, and it is not the same mechanism as the collinear grouping (a curve is not collinear, and merging a curve into a straight line would be a lie).
theDesign.part4_rearAndCornerOnLogicalEdges: the rear is chosen among LOGICAL edges (normal opposition, computed on the line's own direction), then expanded to all its chords; the same-street corner-clip and side_corner rules are evaluated per logical edge too, so a 3 m artifact chord can never be asked to inset 4.57 m again. The three bespoke rules keep their existing text and their existing thresholds; what changes is the index space they are computed in.
theDesign.part5_namedDecline: LabelEdgesDeclineReason gains 'ring-validation-failed'. A ring that fails validation or whose scrub cannot yield >= 3 vertices returns it, never an empty label set. That is the dispatch's item 5 and it is what P-249 relies on.
theDesign.indexSpaceIsPreserved_ThisIsTheCompatibi: output edgeLabels stay aligned to the ORIGINAL raw ring index order (the existing tests assert exact raw indices and the production caller at boundary-primitive/compute.ts:151 insets edge-by-edge against the same ring), so grouping affects WHICH ROLE a chord gets, never the numbering. This is why the 714 Spring, 80577/80578, 34177 and R30 fixtures are expected to stay byte-identical: none of them has a collinear run.

knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully.theClaimRevertHole: Recorded in seatNote. A lane claim is local file state and a `git checkout --` during worktree reconciliation destroys it silently. Worth a durable lesson: reconcile BEFORE claiming, or re-check the claim after any checkout that touches _catalog.
knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully.theDispatchIsWrongTwiceOnTheFactsIWasGiv: The dispatch's defect sentence says the front comes from the nearest street centerline rather than the situs-named street (measured: false on this ring, the situs path wins), and says LDT's labeller groups ring chords into logical edges (measured: it does not; it excludes slivers and refuses shape-only ambiguity instead). Both are recorded as contradictions with the measurement that settles them, because a close that restates the dispatch's prose as if it were my finding is exactly the failure mode DEV_PROCESS is written against.
knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully.midpointDistanceIsTheRealBlindSpot: minDistanceEdgeToPolyline measures the edge MIDPOINT only. A 47 m lot line whose far end touches a street measures 32 m and is invisible at the 25 m threshold. This lane does NOT change that rule (it is A-177-adjacent and out of scope), but the leniency it creates on long lines is why the same-street corner-clip rule had to grow the distance-parity guard, and it is named here so the next reader does not rediscover it.
knownTrapsIAmReadingCarefully.noStoreNoCredentials: This environment holds no serving-store credential and this lane needs none; every fixture is a live public read, reproducible from the URL and the timestamp in the fixture file.
